_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::electrochemistry#1, and the execution that FALSIFIED it. The entry said MATID in SCALAR TRANSPORT DYNAMIC must reference the MAT_matlist and that pointing it at a MAT_ion aborts with 'expected matlist, got ion' from 4C_scatra_factory.cpp. Measured on upstream elch_2D_tertiary_twoEqu_ENC_varParams_ndb_2iter: MATID: 3 (a MAT_ion) runs and passes all ten result tests, and so does the deck with the MATID line deleted — the key is inert here (4C documents it as the material for automatic mesh generation). The load-bearing reference is the ELEMENT LINE's 'MAT <id>': repointing that at a MAT_ion on upstream elch_1D_10ele_3ions_stab_fdcheck aborts with 'Invalid material type!' from src/scatra_ele/4C_scatra_ele_calc_service_elch_NP.cpp inside check_elch_element_parameter. Neither the quoted text nor the file it was attributed to appears (CLAIMED_EXPECTED_MATLIST_TEXT=0, CLAIMED_SCATRA_FACTORY_FILE=0). Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology from the element arm: leave the element lines pointing at the matlist. 'Invalid material type!' disappears, EXIT_ELEMENT_MAT_ION becomes 0 and the fixture must go red.

make the inertness claim untestable: leave MATID pointing at the matlist. The arm then demonstrates nothing about a mis-pointed MATID; ELEMENT_LINES_REPOINTED is unaffected but the mutated sed no longer produces the ion-pointed deck, so the fixture must go red.
